name: The arrival joust
text: A jousting list in a carnival city built entirely from painted wooden planks, canvas and rope: tall flat painted false-front facades like a frontier boomtown, striped tents, bunting, raised plank boardwalks. No stone buildings, no castles, no towers anywhere. Mid-gallop, a lance has punched through a knight's throat; he is flung backwards out of his saddle in a spray of blood, his helmet flying off. The packed crowd on the boardwalk cheers wildly, raising tankards, delighted. In the foreground, one traveller in plain road clothes grips the rail and stares in horror, the only face not cheering. Hot, humid, lush river-delta light.

name: The self-crowned emperor
text: Head-and-shoulders portrait of a grotesquely overfed middle-aged man who has crowned himself emperor: bloated, greasy, several chins, sweat running down his face. His crown is obviously brand new and fake: bright, shiny, gaudy gold, far too big, slipping down crookedly onto his sweaty brow, with fake 'antique' engravings. Furs, heaps of gold chains, a ring on every finger, jewels piled on past all taste. His pose is a stiff, over-rehearsed copy of a royal portrait, chin raised and hand on chest, but his eyes dart sideways in panic. Not dignified, not a real king: a frightened man in a costume. Gaudy torchlit hall behind him.

name: The mage city
text: A city on a flat-topped desert mesa under a hard blue sky. The mesa and the whole city are pale: bone-white stone, sand-coloured fused glass and translucent blue-white crystal, no red rock. Sleek, flowing, gravity-defying towers in the spirit of Zaha Hadid: spires too slender to stand, cantilevers over nothing, a library whose upper floors are wider than its base. Floating bridges and disconnected floating staircases hang in mid-air between the towers. At the centre, a large ornate building with a smooth, seamless facade: no doors, no windows, no openings of any kind. Far below, tiny at the foot of the mesa's cliffs, a cluster of humble round mud-brick domes. Empty desert to the horizon.

name: The orb and the left shoe
text: Comedy scene. A vain, elderly mage in rich robes and a skullcap stands before a glowing crystal orb on a plinth, solemnly offering it his own left shoe, held out reverently in both hands. His left foot is lifted off the floor in just a stocking, shoeless; his right foot still wears its shoe. His face is utterly serious. Behind him at a high curved bench sit two more elderly mages: a prim woman fussing with a scroll, and a drowsy old man nodding off. Beside the orb, a faint transparent ripple in the air like heat haze. The chamber is bright, pale and sleek: smooth white curving walls of fused glass and bone-coloured stone, flowing like Zaha Hadid architecture, lit by daylight. No torches, no dark stone, no wigs. Only these three people in the room: no other figures, silhouettes or shadows of people.

name: The elven plateau
text: A vast flat-topped mountain plateau rising out of a mountain range, its sheer cliffs rooted solidly to the mountains below, not floating. On its summit, a still, mirror-like sacred lake ringed by an elven capital in the manner of Gaudí's Sagrada Família: tall porous stone spires shaped like honeycomb, bones and melting candle wax, encrusted with carved stone fruit, shells and leaves, warm sandstone and bright mosaic tile. Carved stone, not plants or vines. Manicured ornamental gardens and terraced vineyards. A graceful Greek-style stone aqueduct carries the lake's water into the city's fountains. Lower down the mountainside, in haze, a separate church city clings to the slope.

name: The great hall and the wall of names
text: Interior of a northern great hall in deep winter, everything patched and repaired: walls of mismatched planks of different ages and colours, new pale timber lashed with rope to old blackened beams, animal hides nailed over holes in the walls, a gap stuffed with fur, crooked repairs everywhere. Nothing neat or well made. Stone only at the base. A long central fire pit is the only warmth. Antlers, furs and beast skulls hang as trophies; drying herbs and roots hang from the rafters; runes are carved on the beams; bone charms hang by the door. One whole wall is a smoke-darkened timber board carved top to bottom with rows of runic names. Palette of dark browns, greys, black, undyed wool and bone-white; nothing dyed.

name: The rooted city wakes
text: Action shot. A heavy wooden table is flying through the air straight at the viewer, legs first, hurled by thick pale roots that whip up out of the floor; motion lines, spores bursting off it in clouds. Behind it, a vast underground city in a cavern: streets and tiers of buildings made of brass-and-iron machinery, gears, pistons, pipes and great clockwork engines, receding into the distance, all half-swallowed by pale roots, vines and furred grey fungus. Faint lights still glow; a few gears still turn. Nearby, a chair rears up on its back legs and a ceiling fan blade swings down, both driven by vines.

name: The skin comes off
text: Body horror. Facing the viewer in a torchlit witch's den, a kindly-faced old village healer in fur and undyed wool is splitting open down the middle; the gentle, smiling human face is peeling half away and sliding down like a loose mask. Bursting out of the skin, a towering chimera built from mismatched human and animal parts fused together by raw flesh: several human arms of different sizes and skin tones, a goat's leg, a mouth in its chest full of tongues, an extra jaw, a few tentacles, joints bending the wrong way. Wet, pale and sinewy; not a demon, no horns, no wings. The empty human skin hangs off it like a coat. The den: low timber and stone, drying herbs, bone charms. On the floor, a ring of carved Norse runes; no pentagram, no star.
